title: enhance-schema-enforcement-layer-with-granular-errors-and-stream-resilience
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a schema enforcement layer that emits granular error codes and supports streaming-safe soft-fallbacks; improves OpenAI-compat error mapping and adds observability hooks for schema regressions.
commits: a1c3f9b: introduce schema enforcement facade and new error type hierarchy
b2d4e7f: streaming: implement prefix-reconstruction and buffered-validation path
c3e9a2d: openai-compat: map schema errors to compat error codes and add header hints
d4f0b1a: telemetry: add schema_failure_count and validation_latency metrics
e5a7c8b: tests: add unit and e2e coverage for streaming soft-fallbacks
description:
Context and motivation:
User-facing structured-output (response_format) runs into two practical problems in the wild: 1) streaming generation can produce transient schema-invalid partial chunks that later resolve, and 2) strict schema enforcement today results in opaque error messages that make it hard for integrators to choose a mitigation (retry, fallback, coercion). This PR introduces a new schema enforcement layer that aims to: provide actionable, machine-readable error diagnostics; avoid unnecessary hard failures during streaming; and keep the OpenAI-compat layer aligned with Redwood's error codes and guidance.

What this change does (high-level):
- Adds a schema_enforcement facade that sits between generator output and response_format validators. The facade exposes two modes: strict (immediate failure) and streaming-safe (buffer-and-validate with soft-fallback).
- Streaming-safe mode attempts minimal buffering (configurable prefix window) to detect recoverable partial JSON issues and only surface a hard error if final output remains invalid after the window and finalization.
- Introduces a small, well-documented error taxonomy: SCHEMA_COERCION_APPLIED, SCHEMA_TRANSIENT_CHUNK, SCHEMA_FINAL_INVALID, SCHEMA_MISSING_REQUIRED, SCHEMA_TYPE_MISMATCH. These are surfaced in the API error payload and in OpenAI-compat header mapping.
- Improves OpenAI compatibility mapping: errors that would previously surface as generic 400s are now annotated with compat.code and compat.hint fields so client libraries can automatically choose fallback behavior (e.g., re-request with strictness=soft or run post-hoc coercion).
- Adds observability hooks: schema_failure_count, schema_coercion_count, and validation_latency_ms metric tags scoped per-model and per-route.
- Small runtime optimization: validation is incremental and uses cached compiled validators per model+schema to minimize per-request CPU impact.

Files changed (summary):
- server/schema/enforcement_facade.py (new): core facade and modes, prefix buffering logic.
- server/schema/errors.py (new): central error codes and serialization helpers for compat headers.
- server/streaming/validator_adapter.py (modified): integrates buffer window, uses facade for decisioning.
- openai_compat/error_mapper.py (modified): maps new schema codes to compat codes and hints.
- telemetry/metrics.py (modified): new counters and latency histograms.
- docs/api/response_format.md (modified): docs for strict vs streaming-safe behavior and guidance.
- tests/schema/test_streaming_fallbacks.py (new): e2e tests for partial-chunk cases.
- tests/compat/test_error_mapping.py (new): verify compat headers and codes.
- examples/response_format/coercion_demo.ipynb (new): small notebook demonstrating coercion pipeline.
- Makefile / CI configs (tweaks): add schema test stage to e2e pipeline.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Add facade and incremental validators

- [x] Ensure CI green and benchmarks smoke tested (latency impact <4%)

Review highlights / discussion:
- Diego: "Can we make the buffer window configurable per-route and default to a small value (128 tokens)?"
  - Response: yes — default is 256 token-equivalent which we lowered after benchmark runs; route-level override is included in API options.
- Lina: "I'm worried about increased memory usage under high concurrency if many streams buffer simultaneously."
  - Response: we added a global soft cap and an LRU eviction policy for buffer allocations; we also added metrics to instrument buffer pressure.
- Marcus: "OpenAI-compat needs deterministic header names so SDKs can rely on them."
  - Response: headers are now documented and tested (X-Redwood-Compat-Code, X-Redwood-Compat-Hint) and we included mapping from compat.code -> SDK-friendly enum names.
- Security review (internal): no user-supplied schema compilation at runtime; we compile validators server-side and reuse them, reject unsupported schema constructs.

CI / tests summary:
- unit (python): pass
- e2e schema tests (dockerized): pass
- lint (black/isort/flake): pass
- benchmarks (smoke): median validation overhead <3.7% for typical prompt lengths
- full integration tests (flaky network): passed on second run after transient S3 flakiness; CI shows green at merge.

Merge details and follow-ups:
- Merge method: squash and merge. Squash commit summarized as: "schema: enforcement facade + streaming-safe mode; compat error mapping; metrics"
- Follow-up tasks created: ENG-4210 (route-level buffer tuning dashboards), ENG-4235 (SDKs: expose compat enums and automatic fallback helper), PM-97 (docs: migration note for strict=false behavior).

Notes on uniqueness and compatibility: this change does not alter the default behavior for existing customers (strictness defaults to the current server behavior). Customers opting into streaming-safe mode will get richer errors and fewer premature hard failures. The implementation intentionally favors observability and safe defaults; telemetry will allow us to audit how often soft-fallbacks prevent hard failures and whether additional heuristics are required.

If you want to run a quick local repro: see examples/response_format/coercion_demo.ipynb and tests/schema/test_streaming_fallbacks.py.
